name: School Teacher (K–12)
description: School teachers plan and deliver the curriculum, assess what has been learned, manage a classroom and account for every child's progress. ⚠ This page covers elementary, middle, secondary and special education together, because in Florida they share one certification system and differ mainly by which subject examination you sit. ⚠⚠⚠ And it leads with the finding a Florida student most needs: the state ranks around 19th nationally for STARTING pay and 50th for AVERAGE pay. The salary that recruits you is competitive; the one you reach after fifteen years is not.
credentialNote: ⚠ Florida certifies teachers under Chapter 1012 and State Board rules, and there are two certificates. A TEMPORARY certificate is valid for three years and is non-renewable — it exists to let you teach while finishing the requirements. A PROFESSIONAL certificate is valid five years and renewable, and is the real credential. ⚠⚠ The examinations are the Florida Teacher Certification Examinations: the General Knowledge Test, the Professional Education Test, and a SUBJECT AREA EXAMINATION in your certification field. The subject examination is what differs between an elementary teacher and a chemistry teacher; the rest of the process is the same, which is why this page covers them together. ⚠⚠⚠ Florida also runs a genuine ALTERNATIVE route: a bachelor's degree in ANY field, at minimum 2.5 GPA, plus the subject-area examination or appropriate subject coursework, plus employment by a Florida school, gets you a temporary certificate and a classroom. ⚠ Read that as a real option with a real cost — you complete the pedagogy, reading, ESOL and exceptional-student-education requirements while already teaching full time, on a three-year clock that does not stop. ⚠⚠ Add a background check, and note that Florida requires ESOL and reading preparation that many out-of-state programmes do not.
bodyHtml:
Four certification areas, one system

RoleSOC2025 US medianJobsOutlook 2025–35
Kindergarten and elementary teacher25-2021$63,8201,530,500⚠ 0%, −6,100
Special education teacher25-205x$67,170584,100⚠ 0%, −300
Secondary (high school) teacher25-2031$72,0401,087,500⚠ 0%, −2,500

⚠⚠ All of it is flat, and the reason given is enrolment rather than budget: the federal handbook attributes limited demand to declining school enrolments. But the openings are enormous anyway — 37,100 a year in special education alone, almost entirely replacement. The teacher shortage is real and it is a RETENTION problem, not a growth problem. That distinction should shape how you read everything below.

⚠⚠⚠ Florida's pay shape, and it is the most important thing on this page

Florida recruits well and retains badly, and you can see it in two independent sources.

First, the federal wage percentiles. These are the same data for both states, so the comparison is clean:

Elementary teachersFloridaUnited States
10th percentile✅ $48,680$47,960
Median$58,930$63,970
90th percentile⚠⚠ $75,780$104,340
Secondary teachersFloridaUnited States
10th percentile✅ $49,210$48,780
Median$60,410$72,040
90th percentile⚠⚠ $77,100$107,600

⚠⚠⚠ Read the first and last rows together. Florida's FLOOR is above the national floor in both occupations — by $720 for elementary and $430 for secondary. Florida's CEILING is $28,560 below for elementary and $30,500 below for secondary. The state pays beginners slightly better than average and experienced teachers far worse.

Second, the union rankings say the same thing from the other direction. NEA data reported in April 2026 put Florida's average teacher salary at $56,663 — 50th of the 50 states and the District of Columbia — while its average STARTING salary of $49,435 ranked about 19th. The same reporting notes Florida's inflation-adjusted teacher pay is down more than 12% over the past decade.

⚠ Two completely independent sources, one federal and one a union ranking, describing the same compression. This is not a matter of opinion about whether teachers are paid enough; it is a measurable fact about the SHAPE of the Florida scale, and it is the single most useful thing a Florida education student can know before enrolling.

⚠⚠ What to do with it, practically:

  • Do not plan your finances on the starting salary continuing to compare well. It does at year one and it does not at year fifteen.
  • Find out what your target district's salary schedule looks like at step 10 and step 20, not just at step 1. Districts differ substantially and the schedule is public.
  • Look at the routes that pay above the scale — critical-shortage subject supplements, National Board certification, administration, and district or state roles.
  • ⚠ And weigh it honestly against the alternative route below, because if you enter teaching with a subject degree you keep the option of leaving for what that degree pays elsewhere.

⚠⚠ Two routes in, and the second is cheaper and harder

Teacher preparation degreeAlternative certification
What you needa Florida teacher preparation programme⚠ a bachelor's in ANY field, 2.5 GPA, plus the subject examination
When you learn to teachduring the degree, with a supervised internship⚠⚠ while teaching full time
Certificateprofessional, five years, renewabletemporary, three years, NON-renewable
The catchtime and tuition⚠⚠⚠ the three-year clock does not stop

⚠ The alternative route is legitimate and widely used, and Florida designed it deliberately to address shortages. It is also genuinely harder: you complete the pedagogy, reading, ESOL and exceptional-student-education requirements in the evenings and at weekends while running your own classroom for the first time, which is the hardest year of the career. The failure mode is running out the three years.

⚠⚠ Florida requires preparation many states do not — and legislated it

Two Florida requirements catch people who trained elsewhere or came through the alternative route.

ESOL. Florida's English-language-learner population means ESOL preparation is embedded in certification, and it shows in the catalogue: TSL 3080 Foundations of Teaching ESOL in the Schools is carried by 17 institutions and TSL 4081 by 14. This is not an elective here.

⚠⚠⚠ Reading, and this one has statutory force. Florida requires evidence-based reading instruction, mandates K–3 screening and progress monitoring, funds district reading coaches, and has revised both the Reading Endorsement competencies and the B.E.S.T. English Language Arts standards accordingly. So the older “reading as a process” model, three-cueing and guessing from context are not merely out of date in Florida — they are contrary to what the state requires and what the certification examination tests.

⚠ A catalogue title can lag a revised syllabus by years, so judge a reading course by its ASSIGNED TEXT rather than its name — look for Moats, Kilpatrick, Liben, Lindsey or Seidenberg. If a programme is still teaching the older model, its graduates will be underprepared for both the examination and the job. The reading courses to look for are RED 4519 Diagnostic Reading (15 institutions) and the RED sequence generally.

✅ What travels, and the one number that splits

EME 2040 Introduction to Technology for Educators is carried by 33 of the 36 institutions offering its prefix — 92%, one of the best-travelling courses on this site. EDF 1005 Introduction to the Education Profession reaches 23, EEX 2010 Introduction to Exceptional Child Education 18, TSL 3080 17, EDG 4410 Classroom Management 15, RED 4519 15, EDP 2002 Educational Psychology 13.

⚠ The one to watch: Introduction to the Education Profession has two numbers — EDF 1005 at 23 institutions and EDF 2005 at 14. Same course, different level digit. Check which your target programme names.

⚠⚠ And note EEX 2010 at 18 institutions. Exceptional student education content is required of ALL Florida teachers, not only special educators — another requirement that surprises people arriving from out of state.

Necessary skills

  • Classroom management. The skill that determines whether anything else you know can be used, and the commonest reason new teachers leave.
  • Explaining the same thing five different ways. Subject knowledge is necessary and nowhere near sufficient.
  • Assessment and data. Florida's system runs on progress monitoring, and you will be asked to account for it.
  • Reading instruction, on the current evidence base — required of elementary teachers by statute, and useful to every secondary teacher with struggling readers.
  • Differentiation for exceptional students and English learners, both of whom will be in your room whatever you are certified in.
  • Stamina and boundaries. The work expands to fill whatever you give it, and the people who last are the ones who decide where it stops.

Advice

⚠⚠ Look up your target district's full salary schedule before you commit — step 1, step 10 and step 20. Florida's starting pay is competitive nationally and its experienced pay is last in the country, and the schedule is where you will see exactly how that applies to you.

⚠ Consider a shortage area deliberately. Mathematics, science and special education carry supplements in many districts and open the alternative route widest — and special education has 37,100 openings a year nationally against essentially zero growth, which tells you how many people leave it.

⚠ Check the reading courses against the current evidence base, by reading list rather than title. Florida has legislated this and the certification examination follows the legislation.

⚠ If you take the alternative route, count the three years from day one and plan the coursework before you accept the job. The certificate is non-renewable, and the clock is the thing that ends careers before they start.

And get into a classroom before you commit to the degree. Substitute, paraprofessional work, tutoring, a summer programme — anything. Every experienced teacher will tell you that the job is not what it looks like from a desk, and this is one of the few careers where you can find that out for a few weeks' work.

cipCodes.note: Teacher education in specific subject areas — 19 Florida public institutions and 877 credentials. The secondary route, where the subject-area examination you sit defines the certificate.

Special education and teaching — 19 Florida public institutions and 936 credentials. ⚠ Included as a full part of this path rather than an afterthought: it is a shortage area, it has 37,100 annual openings nationally against zero growth, and Florida requires exceptional-student-education content of every teacher.
Education, general — 6 Florida public institutions and 301 credentials, included so programmes filed under the general code appear.

⚠ Business administration, and by extension any bachelor's degree — because Florida's alternative certification route accepts a degree in ANY field plus the subject-area examination. This is a real door into teaching and the reason the path is more open than it looks.

programs.note: The programme itself — 35 Florida public institutions, built around the state certificate rather than merely the degree, so it embeds the reading, ESOL and exceptional-student-education requirements and the supervised internship. ⚠ Read its degrees note on the alternative route, which is the cheaper and harder competitor to it.

⚠ A genuine route via alternative certification — any bachelor's plus the subject-area examination gets a temporary certificate. ⚠⚠ What it skips is the supervised internship and the Florida-specific reading and ESOL preparation, which you then complete while teaching full time on a three-year non-renewable clock.

⚠ A route in for a shortage subject, and worth naming for the trade-off it forces. Mathematics, science and computing degrees open the alternative route widest — and they are also the degrees with the largest gap between Florida teacher pay and what the same qualification earns outside teaching.

courses.reason: Introduction to the Education Profession — 23 institutions. The first course of every Florida teacher preparation route, and it usually carries the first required classroom observation hours.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Carried as EDF2005 at 14 other institutions — same course, different level digit. Check which your target programme names before enrolling.

courses.reason: Introduction to Technology for Educators — 33 of the 36 institutions carrying its prefix, 92%, one of the best-travelling courses on this site. Classroom technology, digital resources and the tools Florida's progress monitoring runs on.
courses.variantNote: ✅ Take it at a state college with complete confidence. Almost nothing in education transfers more reliably.

courses.reason: Introduction to Exceptional Child Education — 18 institutions. ⚠ Required of ALL Florida teachers, not only special educators: every classroom contains students with IEPs and every teacher is accountable for them.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ A Florida requirement that catches people who trained out of state. If you are taking the alternative route, this is one of the things you will be completing while already teaching.

courses.reason: Introduction to Educational Psychology — 13 institutions. How children learn, develop and are motivated — the evidence base behind everything a teacher does deliberately.
Foundations of Teaching ESOL in the Schools — 17 institutions. ⚠ Not an elective in Florida: the state's English-language-learner population means ESOL preparation is embedded in certification.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Followed by TSL4081 TESOL Issues and Practice at 14 institutions. Out-of-state preparation frequently omits this entirely, and it is one of the commonest gaps for teachers moving to Florida.

courses.reason: Diagnostic Reading in the Classroom — 15 institutions. Identifying why a particular child is not reading and choosing the intervention, which Florida requires by statute for K–3.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠⚠ Judge this course by its ASSIGNED TEXT rather than its title. Florida has legislated evidence-based reading instruction and revised the Reading Endorsement competencies and B.E.S.T. standards accordingly — so three-cueing and guessing from context are contrary to what the state requires. Look for Moats, Kilpatrick, Liben, Lindsey or Seidenberg on the reading list.

courses.reason: Classroom Management and Communications — 15 institutions. ⚠ The skill that determines whether everything else you know can be used, and the commonest reason new teachers leave the profession.
Measurement in Education — 14 institutions. Assessment design, score interpretation and progress monitoring — which in Florida is not optional paperwork but the system the state runs on.
Teaching Elementary School Mathematics — 11 institutions. The methods course for the subject most elementary candidates are least confident in, and a Florida shortage area at secondary level.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Elementary candidates should treat this as the hard one. Secondary mathematics has its own methods sequence and its own subject-area examination.

courses.reason: Teaching Science in the Elementary School — 13 institutions. Science methods for generalists, and another Florida shortage subject at secondary level.
Teaching Social Studies in the Elementary School — 11 institutions. The fourth of the elementary methods courses, alongside reading, mathematics and science.
Assessment of Exceptional Education Students — 10 institutions. Eligibility determination, IEP goals and progress monitoring for students with disabilities.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Core for special education candidates, and useful for everyone: general-education teachers sit on IEP teams and are accountable for the goals.

courses.reason: Elementary Education Internship — 11 institutions. The supervised student teaching placement, and the part of the degree the alternative route does not include.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ A full-time placement on the school district's calendar, not the college's, with Level 2 background screening required before entry. ⚠ It is also the single biggest advantage of the degree route over alternative certification: you learn to run a classroom with a mentor in the room rather than alone.

courses.reason: English Composition I — 39 institutions. Required for the degree, and a prerequisite in substance for the General Knowledge Test's English Language Skills and Essay subtests.
College Algebra — 36 institutions. The general-education mathematics most education degrees require, and the content the General Knowledge Test's mathematics subtest assumes.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ The General Knowledge Test is a gate on certification, not merely on the degree. Candidates who scraped through college algebra frequently fail it and have to retake.
